answer: Reputation decay works like a pulse check: each identity's trust score halves every few epochs unless it submits fresh work that random peer juries verify. A sybil farm cannot park thousands of accounts on a knoll of old reputation; idle ones go hollow and lose voting and payout weight. To keep N fakes alive the attacker must pay for N streams of original, graded work every cycle, so cost scales linearly with the fleet while reward per account stays flat.
